text: If this happens tonight... you won't make it three days.
One explosion on the sun... and every light in the world goes out at once.
This isn't a movie. It almost happened... and it can happen again, any day.
Nine P.M. You're watching your phone, just like this... then suddenly, nothing.
No lights. No signal. The whole city goes silent.
A solar storm. Billions of tons of burning gas from the sun... aimed straight at Earth.
Day one. No internet, no calls. You don't know if your family is safe.
The ATMs are dead. Your money... is locked inside the bank.
Day two. The food in your fridge is rotting. Every store is closed.
Then the water stops. Because electricity runs the water too.
Day three. Water, food, and gas run out. This is where the chaos starts.
In hospitals, the last generators are all that's keeping patients alive.
Day seven. The whole world is silent... and for the first time, you can see every star.
But here's the scarier part.
In 1859, the Carrington Event hit. Telegraph wires caught fire, and the northern lights reached the Caribbean.
In 1989, a much weaker storm cut the power to six million people in Quebec.
And in 2012, a storm as strong as Carrington... missed us by just nine days.
